data.title: Verastem: Avutometinib Plus Defactinib Data De-Risk Efficacy Thesis; Buy Rating Reiterated With Unchanged $18 Price Target
data.description:
In a report released today, Andres Y. Maldonado from H.C. Wainwright reiterated a Buy rating on Verastem, with a price target of $18.00.

Andres Y. Maldonado has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors tied to the strength of avutometinib plus defactinib in LGSOC. The newly presented comparative analysis shows that, even after adjusting for key baseline differences, the combination delivers a markedly lower risk of disease progression or death and substantially longer progression-free survival than commonly used therapies, across both KRAS-mutant and KRAS wild-type populations.

He views these results as meaningfully de-risking Verastem’s core efficacy thesis and as a supportive, directional readthrough for the ongoing Phase 3 RAMP 301 trial. In particular, the robust benefit in KRAS-mutant patients and the clinically significant improvement in outcomes for KRAS wild-type disease underpin the potential for label expansion into a much larger commercial population, justifying the continued Buy rating and the unchanged $18 price target.

data.title: CNTB: Buy Rating Reiterated with Unchanged $7 Price Target Ahead of Seabreeze Trial Catalysts
data.description:
H.C. Wainwright analyst Brandon Folkes has reiterated their bullish stance on CNTB stock, giving a Buy rating on August 27.

Brandon Folkes has given his Buy rating due to a combination of factors, most notably the favorable clinical framework emerging around the upcoming Seabreeze trial for asthma and COPD. The key opinion leader highlighted that reducing treatment failure—defined by recurrent exacerbations and repeat acute-care visits—is the outcome that matters most to physicians, patients and payers, with reductions of roughly 30% or more viewed as meaningfully beneficial.

Folkes believes this focus on treatment failure sets a constructive backdrop for rademikibart, as outcomes in the 40–50% reduction range would strongly validate its acute-use strategy. While lung-function metrics like FEV1 remain relevant, he views current investor emphasis on absolute FEV1 gains as overstated given the KOL’s view that more modest improvements can still be clinically important, especially in COPD. As a result, he reiterates a Buy rating on CNTB, with the price target unchanged at $7, reflecting confidence in the upcoming catalyst and the therapy’s potential value.
